claims.claim: Origen was born c. 185, probably in Alexandria, Egypt, and died c. 254 in Tyre, Phoenicia.
Origen was the most important theologian and biblical scholar of the early Greek church.
Origen became head of the Catechetical School of Alexandria, first informally, then officially in 203.
At Ambrose's request, Origen composed the first five books of his Commentary on the Gospel of John.
While teaching in Caesarea, Origen resumed work on his Commentary on John, composing at least books six through ten.
The Commentary on John stands as the beginning of Christian scriptural exegesis.
Origen refutes the Gnostic reading of the Gospel presented by Heracleon, though this polemic is subordinate to his own investigation.
The commentary displays Origen's attention to the literal meaning of passages but moves beyond them to try to grasp their spiritual significance.
This file holds commentary books 13, 19, 20, 28, and 32 only. It is not a continuous run from book 13 to book 32.
Book 13 is the Samaritan woman, book 20 is Abraham's children, book 28 is Lazarus, and book 32 is the washing of the feet.
